findings.text: Provides conversion from kernel virtual address to physical address without debug checks, selecting between an adjustment based on the kernel load base and an adjustment based on the direct map according to whether the input resides in the kernel image mapping.
Aliases the generic physical address helper to the nodebug variant so callers receive identical conversion without extra checking.

Symbol address conversion assumes an input inside the kernel image mapping, enforces an upper bound against the kernel image size in debug builds, then adds the physical load base; relocation hiding is an identity mapping.
Reports maximum task size by choosing between a smaller and a larger address window depending on five level paging availability, using runtime patching keyed on the LA57 feature.
Declares architecture gate area support as present and provides a self alias for the page clearing helper.

Thread, exception and interrupt stack sizes derive from page size shifted by orders that combine base values two, one and two with a KASAN adjustment; the KASAN adjustment has build variants zero and one.
Dedicated interrupt stack indices are DF zero, NMI one, DB two, MCE three and VC four.

The five level direct map base is hex ff11000000000000, the four level direct map base is hex ffff888000000000, the kernel image map base is hex ffffffff80000000, and the generic page offset name aliases the runtime base variable.

Physical mask shift is fifty two; virtual mask shift is fifty six when five level tables are enabled else forty seven; default window is two to the forty seventh power minus one page; maximum task size delegates to the runtime selector.

Thirty two bit compatibility limit is hex c0000000 when the three gigabyte personality is set else hex ffffe000; low task size, full task size, child task size and stack tops select among compatibility limit, default window and runtime maximum based on the ADDR32 thread flag.
Kernel image size has two build variants, one gigabyte and five hundred twelve megabytes.

Virtual mask is one shifted by the virtual shift minus one; physical page, PMD and PUD masks combine the corresponding page masks with the physical mask; huge page geometry follows PMD shift with derived size, mask, order and a maximum of two states; page offset casts the offset constant; default data flags alias the task exec variant.
Kernel load physical address aligns the configured start by the configured alignment; kernel virtual start adds that load address to the kernel map base.
Maximum ioremap mapping order follows PUD shift in one build and PMD shift in another; physical mask aliases a runtime variable in one build and a shift derived mask in the other.
A callee save wrapper carries a single function pointer; the paravirt info record carries an IO delay flag and a name string plus an extra user code segment field under the XXL option.
A no operation pointer aliases the generic nop function, an IO delay query exposes the info flag, and capability setting is an empty inline.
Lock operations record wait and kick callbacks plus a callee save entry for querying virtual CPU preemption, with layout randomization disabled.

Observed CPU operations collect privileged hooks for debug registers, control registers, descriptor tables, TLS, MSRs, counters and context switch under XXL; IRQ operations collect flag save and mask entries plus halt operations; MMU operations collect TLB flush, mmap exit, page encryption status and under XXL CR2 CR3 handling and top level table hooks.

Paravirtual queued lock slow path delegates to a static call and unlock performs a static call trampoline; native unlock uses release ordering, thin wrappers add checking then delegate, preemption query defaults to false without the preemption feature, and wait and kick forward to lock operations.
Virtualized spin lock fast path is gated by a static branch key and otherwise uses a test and set retry loop with processor relaxation, reporting whether it acquired the lock.
TLB helpers forward single user address invalidation and multi processor invalidation with mask and info to MMU operations.
Halt helpers forward safe and normal halt to IRQ operations; stack pointer zero loading forwards to CPU operations.
Debug register access and control register access forward to CPU or MMU operations, with CR2 read and CR3 write offering native instruction alternatives when not under Xen.
MSR read and write including safe variants with error reporting, plus performance counter read, forward to CPU operations; convenience helpers split sixty four bit values into low and high halves.
LDT allocation and release, TR GDT and IDT loading, TR storing, TLS and GS loading, descriptor entry writes and IO bitmap invalidation forward to CPU operations.

Page table top level allocation and release and lower level release and allocation notifications for PTE PMD PUD and P4D forward to MMU operations, with allocation taking the address space and frame number.
Protection modification transaction start returns a PTE value from MMU operations and commit forwards the final value; the architecture transaction capability is declared present.

PUD and P4D value extraction forward to MMU operations with native alternatives when not under Xen; PGD update forwards the native value; PGD clearing applies only when five level tables are enabled; P4D clearing writes a zero entry; native P4D construction wraps the value directly or via PGD depending on build.

Context switch start and end forward to CPU operations; lazy MMU enter is empty while flush and leave forward to MMU flush; fixmap update calls MMU directly; local flag save and interrupt disable and enable forward to IRQ operations with native alternatives when not under Xen, and save combines save plus disable.

Call helpers encode argument passing in fixed registers differing by build, alternative call helpers select between paravirtual and native sequences based on hypervisor and feature conditions, indirect access uses instruction pointer relative dereference, and flag saving selects between paravirtual and native sequences.
Symbol address helper checks only the upper bound and relies on unsigned wrap to catch lower violations, so callers must only pass kernel image addresses.
Virtualized test and set fallback spins without fairness or timeout, so prolonged contention can delay progress.
Architecture halt, interrupt control and TLB flush helpers serve as entry points that transparently dispatch to native sequences or hypervisor operations.
Header guards define unique macros to prevent multiple inclusion for page, paravirt base, spinlock, paravirt and paravirt types headers.
